to0.0pt{\hskip-0.19133pt\raisebox{0.46193pt}[0.0pt]{$\scriptstyle\mathrm{op}$}\hss}\mbox{$\scriptstyle\mathrm{op}$}}}}{\mbox{\uline{\phantom{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{op}$}}\hbox to0.0pt{\hss\color[rgb]{1,1,1}\hbox to0.0pt{\hskip 0.0pt\raisebox{0.5pt}[0.0pt]{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{op}$}\hss}\hbox to0.0pt{\hskip 0.19133pt\raisebox{0.46193pt}[0.0pt]{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{op}$}\hss}\hbox to0.0pt{\hskip 0.35355pt\raisebox{0.35355pt}[0.0pt]{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{op}$}\hss}\hbox to0.0pt{\hskip 0.46193pt\raisebox{0.19133pt}[0.0pt]{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{op}$}\hss}\hbox to0.0pt{\hskip 0.5pt\raisebox{0.0pt}[0.0pt]{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{op}$}\hss}\hbox to0.0pt{\hskip 0.46193pt\raisebox{-0.19133pt}[0.0pt]{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{op}$}\hss}\hbox to0.0pt{\hskip 0.35355pt\raisebox{-0.35355pt}[0.0pt]{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{op}$}\hss}\hbox to0.0pt{\hskip 0.19133pt\raisebox{-0.46193pt}[0.0pt]{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{op}$}\hss}\hbox to0.0pt{\hskip 0.0pt\raisebox{-0.5pt}[0.0pt]{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{op}$}\hss}\hbox to0.0pt{\hskip-0.19133pt\raisebox{-0.46193pt}[0.0pt]{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{op}$}\hss}\hbox to0.0pt{\hskip-0.35355pt\raisebox{-0.35355pt}[0.0pt]{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{op}$}\hss}\hbox to0.0pt{\hskip-0.46193pt\raisebox{-0.19133pt}[0.0pt]{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{op}$}\hss}\hbox to0.0pt{\hskip-0.5pt\raisebox{0.0pt}[0.0pt]{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{op}$}\hss}\hbox to0.0pt{\hskip-0.46193pt\raisebox{0.19133pt}[0.0pt]{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{op}$}\hss}\hbox to0.0pt{\hskip-0.35355pt\raisebox{0.35355pt}[0.0pt]{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{op}$}\hss}\hbox to0.0pt{\hskip-0.19133pt\raisebox{0.46193pt}[0.0pt]{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{op}$}\hss}\mbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{op}$}}}}}}\times\underline{W}),\mathcal{S})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\mathcal{D}}_{W}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f^{*}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces F_{V}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f^{*}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces G_{V}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f_{!}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces F_{W}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f_{*}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces G_{W}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f_{!}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f_{*}}

where all the solid squares commute. We need to show a few things, namely:

•

That the dashed adjoints exist.

•

That
f^{*}:{\mathcal{D}}_{V}\rightarrow{\mathcal{D}}_{W}
preserves
\kappa
-compacts.

•

That
f_{!}\dashv f^{*}
on
\underline{{\mathcal{D}}}
satisfies the left Beck-Chevalley conditions.

To see that the dashed arrows exist, define
f_{!}
to be
F_{V}\circ f_{!}\circ G_{W}
. This works since

\begin{split}\map_{{\mathcal{D}}_{V}}(F_{V}\circ f_{!}\circ G_{W}-,-)&\simeq\map_{\underline{\presheaf}_{{\mathcal{T}}}(\underline{{\mathcal{C}}})_{W}}(G_{W}-,f^{*}\circ G_{V}-)\\
&\simeq\map_{\underline{\presheaf}_{{\mathcal{T}}}(\underline{{\mathcal{C}}})_{W}}(G_{W}-,G_{W}\circ f^{*}-)\\
&\simeq\map_{{\mathcal{D}}_{W}}(-,f^{*}-)\end{split}

To see that
f_{*}
exists, we need to see that
f^{*}
preserves ordinary colimits. For this, we use the description of colimits in Bousfield local subcategories. So let
\varphi:K\rightarrow{\mathcal{D}}_{V}
be a diagram. Then

\begin{split}f^{*}\mathop{colim}\displaylimits_{K\subseteq{\mathcal{D}}_{V}}\varphi&\simeq f^{*}F_{V}\big(\mathop{colim}\displaylimits_{K\subseteq\presheaf_{V}}G_{V}\circ\varphi\big)\\
&\simeq F_{W}f^{*}\big(\mathop{colim}\displaylimits_{K\subseteq\presheaf_{V}}G_{V}\circ\varphi\big)\\
&\simeq F_{W}\big(\mathop{colim}\displaylimits_{K\subseteq\presheaf_{W}}f^{*}\circ G_{V}\circ\varphi\big)\\
&\simeq F_{W}\big(\mathop{colim}\displaylimits_{K\subseteq\presheaf_{W}}G_{W}\circ f^{*}\circ\varphi\big)\\
&=:\mathop{colim}\displaylimits_{K\subseteq{\mathcal{D}}_{W}}f^{*}\circ\varphi\end{split}

And hence
f^{*}
preserves colimits as required, and so by presentability, we obtain a right adjoint
f_{*}
. This completes the first point. Now to see that
f^{*}:{\mathcal{D}}_{V}\rightarrow{\mathcal{D}}_{W}
preserves
\kappa
-compacts, note that
f^{*}:\underline{\presheaf}_{{\mathcal{T}}}(\underline{{\mathcal{C}}})_{V}\rightarrow\underline{\presheaf}_{{\mathcal{T}}}(\underline{{\mathcal{C}}})_{W}
does since
f_{*}:\underline{\presheaf}_{{\mathcal{T}}}(\underline{{\mathcal{C}}})_{W}\rightarrow\underline{\presheaf}_{{\mathcal{T}}}(\underline{{\mathcal{C}}})_{V}
is
\kappa
-accessible by
5.2.7
. Hence since
f^{*}F_{V}\simeq F_{W}f^{*}
, taking right adjoints we get
f_{*}G_{W}\simeq G_{V}f_{*}
. By hypothesis (5),
G
was
\kappa
-accessible and so since it is also fully faithful fibrewise, we get that
f_{*}:{\mathcal{D}}_{W}\rightarrow{\mathcal{D}}_{V}
is
\kappa
-accessible, as required. For the third point, we already know from
3.1.11
that
\underline{{\mathcal{D}}}
is
{\mathcal{T}}
–cocomplete, and so
f_{!}
must
necessarily
give the indexed coproducts which satisfy the left Beck-Chevalley condition by
3.1.9
.

Finally to see (7) implies (1),
3.1.9
says that
\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}
is
{\mathcal{T}}
–cocomplete, and so we are left to show that it is
\kappa
–
{\mathcal{T}}
–accessible. But then this is just because
\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}\simeq\underline{\mathrm{Ind}}_{\kappa}(\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}^{\underline{\kappa}})
by
[
Lur09
, Prop. 5.3.5.12]
(since parametrised-compacts and ind-completion is just fibrewise ordinary compacts/ind-completion because the straightening lands in
\mathrm{Pr}_{L,\kappa}
). This completes the proof for this step and for the theorem.
∎

6.2
The adjoint functor theorem

We now deduce the parametrised version of the adjoint functor theorem from the unparametrised version using characterisation (7) of
6.1.2
. Interestingly, and perhaps instructively, the proof shows us precisely where we need the notion of strong preservation and not just preservation (cf.
3.1.3
and the discussion in
3.2.1
).

Theorem 6.2.1

(Parametrised adjoint functor theorem)
.

Let
F:\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}\rightarrow\underline{{\mathcal{D}}}
be a
{\mathcal{T}}
–functor between
{\mathcal{T}}
–presentable categories. Then:

(1)

If
F
strongly preserves
{\mathcal{T}}
–colimits, then
F
admits a
{\mathcal{T}}
–right adjoint.

(2)

If
F
strongly preserves
{\mathcal{T}}
–limits and is
{\mathcal{T}}
–accessible, then
F
admits a
{\mathcal{T}}
–left adjoint.

Proof.

We want to apply
2.2.7
. To see (1), observe that the ordinary adjoint functor theorem gives us fibrewise right adjoints
F_{V}:{\mathcal{C}}_{V}\rightleftarrows{\mathcal{D}}_{V}:G_{V}
. To see that this assembles to a
{\mathcal{T}}
–functor
G
, we just need to check that the dashed square in the diagram
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\mathcal{C}}_{V}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\mathcal{D}}_{V}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\mathcal{C}}_{W}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\mathcal{D}}_{W}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces F_{V}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f_{!}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f_{!}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces G_{W}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces F_{W}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f^{*}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f^{*}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces G_{W}}

commutes. But then the left adjoints of the dashed compositions are the solid ones, which we know to be commutative by hypothesis that
F
strongly preserves
{\mathcal{T}}
–colimits (and so in particular indexed coproducts, see
3.2.1
). Hence we are done for this case and part (2) is similar.
∎

We will need the following characterisation of functors that strongly preserve
{\mathcal{T}}
–colimits between
{\mathcal{T}}
–presentables in order to understand the correspondence between
{\mathcal{T}}
–presentable categories and small
{\mathcal{T}}
–idempotent-complete ones.

Proposition 6.2.2

(“
[
Lur09
, Prop. 5.5.1.9]
”)
.

Let
f:\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}\rightarrow\underline{{\mathcal{D}}}
be a
{\mathcal{T}}
–functor between
{\mathcal{T}}
–presentables and suppose
\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}
is
\kappa
–
{\mathcal{T}}
–accessible. Then the following are equivalent:

(a)

The functor
f
strongly preserves
{\mathcal{T}}
–colimits

(b)

The functor
f
strongly preserves fibrewise
\kappa
-filtered colimits, and the restriction
f|_{\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}^{\underline{\kappa}}}
strongly preserves
\kappa
–
{\mathcal{T}}
–colimits.

Proof.

That (a) implies (b) is clear since
\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}^{\underline{\kappa}}\subseteq\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}
creates
{\mathcal{T}}
–colimits by
5.1.6
. Now to see (b) implies (a), let
\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}=\underline{\mathrm{Ind}}_{\kappa}(\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}^{\underline{\kappa}})
where
\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}^{\underline{\kappa}}
is
\kappa
–
{\mathcal{T}}
–cocomplete and
{\mathcal{T}}
–idempotent-complete category by
5.1.6
. Now by the proof of (4) implies (5) in
6.1.2
we have a
{\mathcal{T}}
–Bousfield adjunction

L:\underline{\presheaf}(\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}^{\underline{\kappa}})\rightleftarrows\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}:k

Now consider the composite

j^{*}f:\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}^{\underline{\kappa}}\xrightarrow{\>j\>}\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}\xrightarrow{\>f\>}\underline{{\mathcal{D}}}

By the universal property of
{\mathcal{T}}
–presheaves we get a strongly
{\mathcal{T}}
–colimit-preserving functor
F
fitting into the diagram
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}^{\underline{\kappa}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\underline{{\mathcal{D}}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\underline{\presheaf}_{{\mathcal{T}}}(\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}^{\underline{\kappa}})}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces j^{*}f}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces j}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces y}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces k}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces F\coloneqq y_{!}j^{*}f}

We know then that
f\simeq k^{*}y_{!}j^{*}f=k^{*}F
. On the other hand, we can define a functor

F^{\prime}\coloneqq f\circ L\simeq F\circ k\circ L:\underline{\presheaf}_{{\mathcal{T}}}(\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}^{\underline{\kappa}})\longrightarrow\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}\longrightarrow\underline{{\mathcal{D}}}

The
{\mathcal{T}}
–Bousfield adjunction unit
\mathrm{id}_{\underline{\presheaf}_{{\mathcal{T}}}}\Rightarrow k\circ L
gives us a natural transformation

\beta:F\Longrightarrow F^{\prime}=F\circ k\circ L

If we can show that
\beta
is an equivalence then we would be done, since
F
, and so
F^{\prime}=f\circ L
, strongly preserves
{\mathcal{T}}
–colimits. Hence since
L
was a
{\mathcal{T}}
–Bousfield localisation,
f
also strongly preserves
{\mathcal{T}}
–colimits, as required.

To see that
\beta
is an equivalence, let
\underline{\mathcal{E}}\subseteq\underline{\presheaf}_{{\mathcal{T}}}(\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}^{\underline{\kappa}})
be the full
{\mathcal{T}}
–subcategory on which
\beta
is an equivalence. Since both
F
and
F^{\prime}
strongly preserve fibrewise
\kappa
-filtered colimits, we see that
\underline{\mathcal{E}}
is stable under such. Hence it suffices to show that
\underline{\presheaf}_{{\mathcal{T}}}(\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}^{\underline{\kappa}})^{\underline{\kappa}}\subseteq\underline{\mathcal{E}}
since the inclusion will then induce the
{\mathcal{T}}
–functor
\underline{\presheaf}_{{\mathcal{T}}}(\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}^{\underline{\kappa}})\simeq\underline{\mathrm{Ind}}_{\kappa}(\underline{\presheaf}_{{\mathcal{T}}}(\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}^{\underline{\kappa}})^{\underline{\kappa}})\rightarrow\underline{\mathcal{E}}
which is an equivalence by
5.2.1
(2).

Since
L\circ k\simeq\mathrm{id}
we clearly have
\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}^{\underline{\kappa}}\subseteq\underline{\mathcal{E}}
, ie. that
\beta:F\Rightarrow F^{\prime}
is an equivalence on
\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}^{\underline{\kappa}}\subseteq\underline{\presheaf}_{{\mathcal{T}}}(\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}^{\underline{\kappa}})
. On the other hand, by
5.1.6
we know that
\underline{\presheaf}_{{\mathcal{T}}}(\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}^{\underline{\kappa}})^{\underline{\kappa}}
is
\kappa
–
{\mathcal{T}}
–cocomplete, and its objects are retracts of
\kappa
-small
{\mathcal{T}}
–colimits valued in
\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}^{\underline{\kappa}}\subseteq\underline{\presheaf}_{{\mathcal{T}}}(\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}^{\underline{\kappa}})
by
5.2.5
. Thus it suffices to show that
F
and
F^{\prime}
strongly preserve
\kappa
-small
{\mathcal{T}}
–colimits when restricted to
\underline{\presheaf}_{{\mathcal{T}}}(\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}^{\underline{\kappa}})^{\underline{\kappa}}
. That
F
does is clear since it in fact strongly preserves all small
{\mathcal{T}}
–colimits. That
F^{\prime}
does is because it can be written as the composition

F^{\prime}|_{\underline{\presheaf}_{{\mathcal{T}}}(\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}^{\underline{\kappa}})^{\underline{\kappa}}}:\underline{\presheaf}_{{\mathcal{T}}}(\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}^{\underline{\kappa}})^{\underline{\kappa}}\xrightarrow{L}\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}^{\underline{\kappa}}\xrightarrow{f}\underline{{\mathcal{D}}}

where
L
is a
{\mathcal{T}}
–left adjoint and
f
strongly preserves
\kappa
-small
{\mathcal{T}}
–colimits by assumption. Here we have crucially used that
L
lands in
\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}^{\underline{\kappa}}
since this category is
{\mathcal{T}}
–idempotent-complete and
\kappa
–
{\mathcal{T}}
–cocomplete.
∎

6.3
Dwyer-Kan localisations

Terminology 6.3.1
.

We recall the clarifying terminology of
[
Hin16
]
in distinguishing between Bousfield localisations, as defined in
2.2.3
, and
Dwyer-Kan localisations
. By the latter, we will mean the following: let
\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}
be a
{\mathcal{T}}
–category and
S
a class of morphisms in
\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}
such that
f^{*}(S_{W})\subseteq S_{V}
for all
f\colon V\rightarrow W
in
{\mathcal{T}}
. Suppose a
{\mathcal{T}}
–category
S^{-1}\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}
exists and is equipped with a map
f:\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}\rightarrow S^{-1}\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}
inducing the equivalence

f^{*}:\underline{\func}_{{\mathcal{T}}}(S^{-1}\underline{{\mathcal{C}}},\underline{{\mathcal{D}}})\xrightarrow{\simeq}\underline{\func}_{{\mathcal{T}}}^{S^{-1}}(\underline{{\mathcal{C}}},\underline{{\mathcal{D}}})

for all
{\mathcal{T}}
–categories
\underline{{\mathcal{D}}}
, where
\underline{\func}_{{\mathcal{T}}}^{S^{-1}}(\underline{{\mathcal{C}}},\underline{{\mathcal{D}}})\subseteq\underline{\func}_{{\mathcal{T}}}(\underline{{\mathcal{C}}},\underline{{\mathcal{D}}})
is the full subcategory of parametrised functors sending morphisms in
S
to equivalences. Such a
{\mathcal{T}}
–category must necessarily be unique if it exists, and this is then defined to be
the
{\mathcal{T}}
–Dwyer-Kan localisation of

\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}

with respect to

S
. The following proposition shows that being a
{\mathcal{T}}
–Bousfield localisation is stronger than that of being a
{\mathcal{T}}
–Dwyer-Kan localisation.

Proposition 6.3.2

(Bousfield implies Dwyer-Kan)
.

Let
\underline{{\mathcal{C}}},L\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}
be
{\mathcal{T}}
–categories and
L:\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}\rightleftarrows L\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}:i
be a
{\mathcal{T}}
–Bousfield localisation. Let
S
be the collection of morphisms in
\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}
that are sent to equivalences under
L
. Then the functor
L
induces an equivalence

L^{*}:\underline{\func}_{{\mathcal{T}}}(L\underline{{\mathcal{C}}},\underline{{\mathcal{D}}})\xrightarrow{\simeq}\underline{\func}_{{\mathcal{T}}}^{S^{-1}}(\underline{{\mathcal{C}}},\underline{{\mathcal{D}}})

for any
{\mathcal{T}}
–category
\underline{{\mathcal{D}}}
so that
L\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}
is a Dwyer-Kan localisation against
S
.

Proof.

Since
L\dashv i
was a
{\mathcal{T}}
–Bousfield localisation, we know that
i^{*}:\underline{\func}_{{\mathcal{T}}}(L\underline{{\mathcal{C}}},\underline{{\mathcal{D}}})\rightleftarrows\underline{\func}_{{\mathcal{T}}}(\underline{{\mathcal{C}}},\underline{{\mathcal{D}}}):L^{*}
is also a
{\mathcal{T}}
–Bousfield localisation by
3.1.10
, and so in particular
L^{*}
is
{\mathcal{T}}
–fully faithful. The image of
L^{*}
also clearly lands in
\underline{\func}_{{\mathcal{T}}}^{S^{-1}}(\underline{{\mathcal{C}}},\underline{{\mathcal{D}}})
, and so we are left to show
{\mathcal{T}}
–essential surjectivity. By basechanging if necessary, we just show this on
\func_{{\mathcal{T}}}^{S^{-1}}(\underline{{\mathcal{C}}},\underline{{\mathcal{D}}})
. Let
\varphi:\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}\rightarrow\underline{{\mathcal{D}}}
be a
{\mathcal{T}}
–functor that inverts morphisms in
S
. We aim to show that
\varphi\Rightarrow\varphi\circ i\circ L
is an equivalence. Since
L\dashv i
was a
{\mathcal{T}}
–Bousfield localisation, the unit
\eta:\mathrm{id}\Rightarrow i\circ L
gets sent to an equivalence under
L
, and so
\eta\in S
. Since
\varphi
inverts
S
by assumption, in particular it inverts
\eta
.
∎

Proposition 6.3.3
.

{\mathcal{T}}
–presentable categories are
{\mathcal{T}}
–complete.

Proof.

Let
\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}
be
{\mathcal{T}}
–presentable so that it is a
{\mathcal{T}}
–Bousfield localisation of some
{\mathcal{T}}
–presheaf category
\underline{\presheaf}_{{\mathcal{T}}}(\underline{{\mathcal{D}}})
by description (5) of
6.1.2
. We know that
\underline{\presheaf}_{{\mathcal{T}}}(\underline{{\mathcal{D}}})
is
{\mathcal{T}}
–complete and so all we need to show is that
{\mathcal{T}}
–Bousfield local subcategories are closed under
{\mathcal{T}}
–limits which exist in the ambient category. But this is clear since
{\mathcal{T}}
–Bousfield local subcategories can be described by a mapping-into property.
∎

Terminology 6.3.4
.

For
S\subseteq\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}
a collection of morphisms, an object
X\in\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}
is said to be
S
–local if
{\map}_{\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}}(-,X)
sends morphisms in
S
to equivalences.

In fact, as in the unparametrised case, we can give a precise description of maps that get inverted in a Bousfield localisation against an arbitrary collection of morphisms
S
, generalising the usual theory available for instance in
[
Lur09
,
\lx@sectionsign 5.5.4
]
.

Definition 6.3.5
.

Let
\overline{S}
be a
{\mathcal{T}}
–collection of morphisms in a
{{\mathcal{T}}}
–category
\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}
. We say that it is
{{\mathcal{T}}}
–strongly saturated
if the following conditions are satisfied:

1.

(Pushout closure) Suppose we have a fibrewise pushout square in
\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces A}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces B}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces C}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces D.}

\ulcorner

If the left vertical is in
\overline{S}
, then the right vertical is also in
\overline{S}
.

2.

(
{{\mathcal{T}}}
-colimit closure) The
{{\mathcal{T}}}
-full subcategory
\underline{\func}^{\overline{S}}(\Delta^{1},\underline{{\mathcal{C}}})\subseteq\underline{\func}(\Delta^{1},\underline{{\mathcal{C}}})
of morphisms in
\overline{S}
is closed under
{{\mathcal{T}}}
-colimits.

3.

(2-out-of-3) If any two of the three morphisms in
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces A}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces B}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces C}

are in
\overline{S}
, then the third one is too.

For any
{\mathcal{T}}
–collection of morphisms
S
, we define its
{\mathcal{T}}
–strong saturation closure

\overline{S}
to be the smallest
{{\mathcal{T}}}
–collection containing
S
which is
{{\mathcal{T}}}
–strongly saturated.

Proposition 6.3.6
.

Let
\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}
be a
{{\mathcal{T}}}
-presentable category and
S
a
{\mathcal{T}}
–collection of morphisms in
\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}
, and
\overline{S}
its
{{\mathcal{T}}}
-strong saturation. Let
L:\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}\rightarrow L_{S}\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}
be the
{{\mathcal{T}}}
-Bousfield localisation at
S
. Then the collection of
L
-equivalences consists precisely of the collection
\overline{S}
.

Proof.

We will bootstrap the parametrised statement from the unparametrised version in
[
Lur09
, Prop. 5.5.4.15]
. Let
T
be the collection of
L
-equivalences. First of all, note that we have
\overline{S}\subseteq T
since it is straightforward to check that
T
is a
{\mathcal{T}}
–strongly saturated collection containing
S
and
\overline{S}
is by definition the minimal such collection. To see the reverse inclusion, let
f:X\rightarrow Y
be an
L
-equivalence and consider the square
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces X}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces Y}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces LX}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces LY}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces Lf}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\simeq}

Now since a
{\mathcal{T}}
-Bousfield localisation is in particular a fibrewise Bousfield localisation, we can apply
[
Lur09
, Prop. 5.5.4.15 (1)]
to see that the vertical maps in the square are in
\overline{S}
. And hence by 2-out-of-3, we see that
f
was also in
\overline{S}
, as desired.
∎

The following result, which will be crucial for our application in
[
Hil22a
]
, is another example of the value of characterisation (7) from
6.1.2
. The proof of the unparametrised result, given by Lurie in
[
Lur09
,
\lx@sectionsign 5.5.4
]
, is long and technical, and characterisation (7) allows us to obviate this difficulty by bootstrapping from Lurie’s statement.

Theorem 6.3.7

(Parametrised presentable Dwyer-Kan localisations)
.

Let
\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}
be a
{\mathcal{T}}
-presentable category and
S
a small collection of
\>{{\mathcal{T}}}
-morphisms of
\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}
(ie. if
f:V\rightarrow W
in
{\mathcal{T}}
and
y\rightarrow z
a morphism in
S_{W}
, then
f^{*}y\rightarrow f^{*}z
is in
S_{V}
). Then:

(1)

Writing
S_{\underline{\amalg}}\supset S
for the closure of
S
under finite indexed coproducts, the fibrewise full subcategory
S^{-1}_{\underline{\amalg}}\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}\subseteq\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}
of
S_{\underline{\amalg}}
-local objects assembles to a
{\mathcal{T}}
–full subcategory.

(2)

We have a
{\mathcal{T}}
–accessible
{\mathcal{T}}
–Bousfield localisation

L:\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}\rightleftarrows S^{-1}_{\underline{\amalg}}\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}:i
.

(3)

For any
{\mathcal{T}}
–category
\underline{{\mathcal{D}}}
, the
{\mathcal{T}}
–functor
L^{*}:\underline{\func}^{L}_{{\mathcal{T}}}(S^{-1}_{\underline{\amalg}}\underline{{\mathcal{C}}},\underline{{\mathcal{D}}})\longrightarrow\underline{\func}^{L,\overline{S}^{-1}}_{{\mathcal{T}}}(\underline{{\mathcal{C}}},\underline{{\mathcal{D}}})
is an equivalence. Moreover, the inclusion
\underline{\func}^{L,\overline{S}^{-1}}_{{\mathcal{T}}}(\underline{{\mathcal{C}}},\underline{{\mathcal{D}}})\subseteq\underline{\func}^{L,S^{-1}}_{{\mathcal{T}}}(\underline{{\mathcal{C}}},\underline{{\mathcal{D}}})
is an equivalence.

Proof.

For (1), we just nee to show that
S^{-1}_{\underline{\amalg}}\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}
is closed under the restriction functors in
\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}
. Let
f\colon V\rightarrow W
be a map in
{\mathcal{T}}
and let
x\in(S^{-1}_{\underline{\amalg}}\underline{{\mathcal{C}}})_{W}
. We need to show that
f^{*}x\in(S^{-1}_{\underline{\amalg}}\underline{{\mathcal{C}}})_{V}
is again
S_{\underline{\amalg}}
–local. So let
\varphi\colon a\rightarrow b
be a morphism in
S_{\underline{\amalg}}
. Because
S_{\underline{\amalg}}
is closed under finite indexed coproducts, we have the equivalence

{\map}_{V}(b,f^{*}x)\simeq{\map}_{W}(f_{!}b,x)\xrightarrow[\simeq]{(f_{!}\varphi)^{*}}{\map}_{W}(f_{!}a,x)\simeq{\map}_{V}(a,f^{*}x)

as wanted.
For (2), we know from
[
Lur09
, Prop. 5.5.4.15]
that we already have fibrewise Bousfield localisations, and all we need to do is show that these assemble to a
{\mathcal{T}}
–Bousfield localisation via
2.2.7
. Let
f:V\rightarrow W
be in
{\mathcal{T}}
. We need to show that
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\mathcal{C}}_{V}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces S^{-1}_{\underline{\amalg}}{\mathcal{C}}_{V}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\mathcal{C}}_{W}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces S^{-1}_{\underline{\amalg}}{\mathcal{C}}_{W}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces L_{V}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces L_{W}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f^{*}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f^{*}}

commutes, and for this, we first note that the diagram
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\mathcal{C}}_{V}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces S^{-1}_{\underline{\amalg}}{\mathcal{C}}_{V}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces{\mathcal{C}}_{W}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces S^{-1}_{\underline{\amalg}}{\mathcal{C}}_{W}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f_{*}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces i_{V}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f_{*}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces i_{W}}

commutes where here
f_{*}
exists since
\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}
is
{\mathcal{T}}
–complete by
6.3.3
. Now recall by definition that
f^{*}(S_{W})\subseteq S_{V}
and so
for
y\rightarrow z
in
S_{W}
the map

\map_{W}(z,f_{*}x)\simeq\map_{V}(f^{*}z,x)\longrightarrow\map_{V}(f^{*}y,x)\simeq\map_{V}(y,f_{*}x)

is an equivalence, which implies that
f_{*}
takes
S_{\underline{\amalg}}
-local objects to
S_{\underline{\amalg}}
-local objects. Now by uniqueness of left adjoints, the first diagram commutes, as required. Finally, the first sentence of (3) is just a consequence of
6.3.2
and
6.3.6
, noting also that
\overline{S}=\overline{S}_{\underline{\amalg}}
. That the inclusion is an equivalence is because if
F\in\underline{\func}^{L,S^{-1}}_{{\mathcal{T}}}(\underline{{\mathcal{C}}},\underline{{\mathcal{D}}})
and we have a morphism in
\overline{S}
of the form
\underline{\mathop{colim}\displaylimits}_{\underline{J}}\varphi\colon\underline{\mathop{colim}\displaylimits}_{\underline{J}}a\rightarrow\underline{\mathop{colim}\displaylimits}_{\underline{J}}b
for some
\underline{J}
–indexed diagram of morphisms all landing in
S
, then
F\underline{\mathop{colim}\displaylimits}_{\underline{J}}\varphi\simeq\underline{\mathop{colim}\displaylimits}_{\underline{J}}F\varphi
is an equivalence by the hypothesis on
F
.
∎

6.4
Localisation–cocompletions

In this subsection we formulate and prove the construction of
localisation–cocompletions
whose proof is exactly analogous to that of
[
Lur09
]
. As far as we can see, unfortunately the proof cannot be bootstrapped from the unparametrised statement as with the proof of
6.3.7
because the notion of a parametrised collection of diagrams might involve diagrams that are not fibrewise in the sense of
Example

3.1.2
.

Definition 6.4.1

(Parametrised collection of diagrams)
.

Let
\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}\in\mathrm{Cat}_{{\mathcal{T}}}
. A
parametrised collection of diagrams in

\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}
is defined to be a triple
(\underline{{\mathcal{C}}},\mathcal{K},\mathcal{R})
where:

•

\mathcal{K}
is a collection of small categories parametrised over
{\mathcal{T}}^{\mathrm{op}}
, ie. a collection
\mathcal{K}_{V}
of small
{\mathcal{T}}_{/V}
–categories for each
V\in{\mathcal{T}}
.

•

\mathcal{R}
is a parametrised collection of diagrams in
\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}
whose indexing categories belong to
\mathcal{K}
, ie. for each
V\in{\mathcal{T}}
a collection of coconed diagrams
\mathcal{R}_{V}
indexed over categories in
\mathcal{K}_{V}
.

Theorem 6.4.2

(
{\mathcal{T}}
–localisation–cocompletions, “
[
Lur09
, Prop. 5.3.6.2]
”)
.

Let
(\underline{{\mathcal{C}}},\mathcal{K},\mathcal{R})
be a parametrised collection of diagrams in
\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}
. Then there is a
{\mathcal{T}}
–category
\underline{\presheaf}^{\mathcal{K}}_{\mathcal{R}}(\underline{{\mathcal{C}}})
and a
{\mathcal{T}}
–functor
j:\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}\rightarrow\underline{\presheaf}^{\mathcal{K}}_{\mathcal{R}}(\underline{{\mathcal{C}}})
such that:

1.

The category
\underline{\presheaf}^{\mathcal{K}}_{\mathcal{R}}(\underline{{\mathcal{C}}})
is
\mathcal{K}
–
{\mathcal{T}}
–cocomplete, ie. it strongly admits
\mathcal{K}
–indexed
{\mathcal{T}}
–colimits,
\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}_{\underline{V}}
admits
K
–indexed
{\mathcal{T}}_{/V}
–colimits.

2.

For every
\mathcal{K}
-
{\mathcal{T}}
–cocomplete category
\underline{{\mathcal{D}}}
, the map
j
induces an equivalence of
{\mathcal{T}}
–categories

j^{*}:\underline{\func}_{{\mathcal{T}}}^{\mathcal{K}}(\underline{\presheaf}^{\mathcal{K}}_{\mathcal{R}}(\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}),\underline{{\mathcal{D}}})\longrightarrow\underline{\func}_{{\mathcal{T}}}^{\mathcal{R}}(\underline{{\mathcal{C}}},\underline{{\mathcal{D}}})

where the source denotes the
{\mathcal{T}}
–category of functors which strongly preserve
\mathcal{K}
–indexed colimits and the target consists of those functors carrying each diagram in
\mathcal{R}
to a parametrised colimit diagram in
\underline{{\mathcal{D}}}
.

3.

If each member of
\mathcal{R}
were already a
{\mathcal{T}}
–colimit diagram in
\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}
, then in fact
j
is
{\mathcal{T}}
–fully faithful.

Proof.

We give first all the constructions. By enlarging the universe, if necessary, we may reduce to the case where:

•

Every element of
\mathcal{K}
is small

•

That
\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}
is small

•

The collection of diagrams
\mathcal{R}
is small

Let
y:\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}\hookrightarrow\underline{\presheaf}_{{\mathcal{T}}}(\underline{{\mathcal{C}}})
be the
{\mathcal{T}}
–yoneda embedding and let
V\in{\mathcal{T}}
. For a
{\mathcal{T}}_{/V}
–diagram
\bar{p}:K^{\underline{\triangleright}}\rightarrow\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}_{\underline{V}}
with cone point
Y
, let
X
denote the
{\mathcal{T}}_{/V}
–colimit of
y\circ p:K\rightarrow\underline{\presheaf}_{{\mathcal{T}}}(\underline{{\mathcal{C}}})_{\underline{V}}
. This induces a
{\mathcal{T}}_{/V}
–morphism in
\underline{\presheaf}_{{\mathcal{T}}}(\underline{{\mathcal{C}}})_{\underline{V}}

s:X\rightarrow y(Y)

Here we have used that
\underline{\presheaf}_{{\mathcal{T}}}(\underline{{\mathcal{C}}})_{\underline{V}}\simeq\underline{\presheaf}_{\underline{V}}(\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}_{\underline{V}})
by
2.1.13
. Now let
S
be the set of all such
{\mathcal{T}}_{/V}
–morphisms running over all
V\in{\mathcal{T}}
. This is small by our assumption and so let
L:\underline{\presheaf}_{{\mathcal{T}}}(\underline{{\mathcal{C}}})\rightarrow S^{-1}\underline{\presheaf}_{{\mathcal{T}}}(\underline{{\mathcal{C}}})
denote the
{\mathcal{T}}
–Bousfield localisation from
6.3.7
. Now we define
\underline{\presheaf}_{\mathcal{R}}^{\mathcal{K}}(\underline{{\mathcal{C}}})\subseteq S^{-1}\underline{\presheaf}_{{\mathcal{T}}}(\underline{{\mathcal{C}}})
to be the smallest
\mathcal{K}
–cocomplete full
{\mathcal{T}}
–subcategory containing the image of
L\circ y:\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}\rightarrow\underline{\presheaf}_{{\mathcal{T}}}(\underline{{\mathcal{C}}})\rightarrow S^{-1}\underline{\presheaf}_{{\mathcal{T}}}(\underline{{\mathcal{C}}})
. We show that this works and prove each point in turn.

Point (i) is true by construction, and so there is nothing to do. For point (ii), let
\underline{{\mathcal{D}}}
be
\mathcal{K}
–
{\mathcal{T}}
–cocomplete. We now perform a reduction to the case when
\underline{{\mathcal{D}}}
is
{\mathcal{T}}
–cocomplete. By taking the opposite Yoneda embedding we see that
\underline{{\mathcal{D}}}
sits
{\mathcal{T}}
–fully faithfully in a
{\mathcal{T}}
–cocomplete category
\underline{{\mathcal{D}}}^{\prime}
and the inclusion strongly preserves
\mathcal{K}
–colimits. We now have a square of
{\mathcal{T}}
–categories (where the vertical functors are
{\mathcal{T}}
–fully faithful by
3.4.6
)
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\underline{\func}_{{\mathcal{T}}}^{\mathcal{K}}(\underline{\presheaf}^{\mathcal{K}}_{\mathcal{R}}(\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}),\underline{{\mathcal{D}}})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\underline{\func}_{{\mathcal{T}}}^{\mathcal{R}}(\underline{{\mathcal{C}}},\underline{{\mathcal{D}}})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\underline{\func}_{{\mathcal{T}}}^{\mathcal{K}}(\underline{\presheaf}^{\mathcal{K}}_{\mathcal{R}}(\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}),\underline{{\mathcal{D}}}^{\prime})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\underline{\func}_{{\mathcal{T}}}^{\mathcal{R}}(\underline{{\mathcal{C}}},\underline{{\mathcal{D}}}^{\prime})}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\phi\coloneqq j^{*}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\phi^{\prime}\coloneqq j^{*}}

We claim this is cartesian in
\widehat{\mathrm{Cat}}_{{\mathcal{T}}}
if
\phi^{\prime}
were an equivalence: given this, to prove that
\phi
is an equivalence, it suffices to prove that
\phi^{\prime}
is an equivalence. For this, we need to show that the map into the pullback is an equivalence. That
\phi^{\prime}
is an equivalence ensures that the map into the pullback is fully faithful. To see essential surjectivity, let
F:\underline{\presheaf}^{\mathcal{K}}_{\mathcal{R}}(\underline{{\mathcal{C}}})\rightarrow\underline{{\mathcal{D}}}^{\prime}
be a strongly
\mathcal{K}
–colimit preserving functor that restricts to
\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}\rightarrow\underline{{\mathcal{D}}}
. Then in fact
F
lands in
\underline{{\mathcal{D}}}\subseteq\underline{{\mathcal{D}}}^{\prime}
since
\underline{{\mathcal{D}}}\subseteq\underline{{\mathcal{D}}}^{\prime}
is stable under
\mathcal{K}
–indexed colimits, and by construction,
\underline{\presheaf}^{\mathcal{K}}_{\mathcal{R}}({\mathcal{C}})
is generated under
\mathcal{K}
–indexed colimits by
\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}
.

Now we turn to showing
\phi
is an equivalence in the case
\underline{{\mathcal{D}}}
is
{\mathcal{T}}
–cocomplete. Let
\underline{\mathcal{E}}\subseteq\underline{\presheaf}_{{\mathcal{T}}}(\underline{{\mathcal{C}}})
be the inverse image
L^{-1}\underline{\presheaf}^{\mathcal{K}}_{\mathcal{R}}(\underline{{\mathcal{C}}})
and
\overline{S}
be the collection of all morphisms
\alpha
in
\underline{\mathcal{E}}
such that
L\alpha
is an equivalence. Since the
{\mathcal{T}}
–Bousfield localisation
L:\underline{\presheaf}(\underline{{\mathcal{C}}})\rightleftarrows S^{-1}\underline{\presheaf}(\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}):i
induces a
{\mathcal{T}}
–Bousfield localisation
L:\underline{\mathcal{E}}\rightleftarrows\underline{\presheaf}^{\mathcal{K}}_{\mathcal{R}}(\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}):i
we see by
6.3.2
that
L^{*}:\underline{\func}_{{\mathcal{T}}}(\underline{\presheaf}^{\mathcal{K}}_{\mathcal{R}}(\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}),\underline{{\mathcal{D}}})\rightarrow\underline{\func}_{{\mathcal{T}}}^{\overline{S}^{-1}}(\underline{\mathcal{E}},\underline{{\mathcal{D}}})
is an equivalence. Furthermore, by using the description of colimits in
{\mathcal{T}}
–Bousfield local subcategories as being given by applying the localisation
L
to the colimit in the ambient category, we see that
f:\underline{\presheaf}^{\mathcal{K}}_{\mathcal{R}}(\underline{{\mathcal{C}}})\rightarrow\underline{{\mathcal{D}}}
strongly preserves
\mathcal{K}
–colimits if and only if
f\circ L:\underline{\mathcal{E}}\rightarrow\underline{{\mathcal{D}}}
does. This gives us the following factorisation of
\phi

\phi:\underline{\func}_{{\mathcal{T}}}^{\mathcal{K}}(\underline{\presheaf}^{\mathcal{K}}_{\mathcal{R}}(\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}),\underline{{\mathcal{D}}})\xrightarrow[\simeq]{L^{*}}\underline{\func}_{{\mathcal{T}}}^{\overline{S}^{-1},\mathcal{K}}(\underline{\mathcal{E}},\underline{{\mathcal{D}}})\xrightarrow{j^{*}}\underline{\func}_{{\mathcal{T}}}^{\mathcal{R}}(\underline{{\mathcal{C}}},\underline{{\mathcal{D}}})

and hence we need to show that the functor
j^{*}
is an equivalence. Since
\underline{{\mathcal{D}}}
is
{\mathcal{T}}
–cocomplete, we can consider the
{\mathcal{T}}
–adjunction

j_{!}:\underline{\func}_{{\mathcal{T}}}^{\mathcal{R}}(\underline{{\mathcal{C}}},\underline{{\mathcal{D}}})\rightleftarrows\underline{\func}_{{\mathcal{T}}}^{\mathcal{K}}(\underline{\mathcal{E}},\underline{{\mathcal{D}}}):j^{*}
. We need to show:

•

that
j_{!}
lands in
\underline{\func}_{{\mathcal{T}}}^{\overline{S}^{-1},\mathcal{K}}(\underline{\mathcal{E}},\underline{{\mathcal{D}}})
,

•

that
j_{!}\circ j^{*}\simeq\mathrm{id}
on
\underline{\func}_{{\mathcal{T}}}^{\overline{S}^{-1},\mathcal{K}}(\underline{\mathcal{E}},\underline{{\mathcal{D}}})
and
j^{*}\circ j_{!}\simeq\mathrm{id}.

For the first point, fix a
V\in{\mathcal{T}}
. Since relative adjunctions are closed under pullbacks by
2.2.4
and since
\underline{\func}_{{\mathcal{T}}}(\underline{{\mathcal{C}}},\underline{{\mathcal{D}}})_{\underline{V}}\simeq\underline{\func}_{\underline{V}}(\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}_{\underline{V}},\underline{{\mathcal{D}}}_{\underline{V}})
by
2.1.13
, we also get a
{\mathcal{T}}_{/V}
-adjunction

j_{!}:\underline{\func}_{\underline{V}}^{\mathcal{R}_{\underline{V}}}(\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}_{\underline{V}},\underline{{\mathcal{D}}}_{\underline{V}})\rightleftarrows\underline{\func}_{\underline{V}}^{\mathcal{K}_{\underline{V}}}(\underline{\mathcal{E}}_{\underline{V}},\underline{{\mathcal{D}}}_{\underline{V}}):j^{*}
. Suppose
F:\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}_{\underline{V}}\rightarrow\underline{{\mathcal{D}}}
is a
{\underline{V}}
–functor that sends
\mathcal{R}_{\underline{V}}
to
{\underline{V}}
–colimit diagrams. We want to show that
j_{!}F:\underline{\mathcal{E}}_{\underline{V}}\rightarrow\underline{{\mathcal{D}}}_{\underline{V}}
inverts maps in
\overline{S}
, ie. those maps that get inverted by
L_{\underline{V}}
. Consider
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}_{\underline{V}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\underline{\mathcal{E}}_{\underline{V}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\underline{{\mathcal{D}}}_{\underline{V}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\underline{\presheaf}_{\underline{V}}(\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}_{\underline{V}})}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces j}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces F}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces y}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces k}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces y_{!}F}

Note that
j_{!}F\simeq k^{*}y_{!}F
since
j_{!}=\mathrm{id}\circ j_{!}\simeq k^{*}k_{!}j_{!}\simeq k^{*}y_{!}
. Now since
y_{!}F:\underline{\presheaf}_{\underline{V}}(\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}_{\underline{V}})\rightarrow\underline{{\mathcal{D}}}_{\underline{V}}
strongly preserves
{\underline{V}}
–colimits and since
\underline{\mathcal{E}}_{\underline{V}}
is stable under
\mathcal{K}
–indexed colimits in
\underline{\presheaf}_{\underline{V}}(\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}_{\underline{V}})
(since

–colimits by construction) it follows that

strongly preserves
\mathcal{K}
–colimits. Now note that the maps in
S\subseteq\underline{\presheaf}_{\underline{V}}(\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}_{\underline{V}})
are inverted by

since these were the maps comparing colimit in
\underline{\presheaf}_{\underline{V}}(\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}_{\underline{V}})
and cone point in
\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}_{\underline{V}}
, and by hypothesis,
F
, and hence
y_{!}F
turns these into equivalences. Therefore, by the universal property of Dwyer-Kan localisations

,
y_{!}F:\underline{\presheaf}_{\underline{V}}(\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}_{\underline{V}})\rightarrow\underline{{\mathcal{D}}}

, and so in particular inverts

, so that

does too. Also

strongly preserves all
{\underline{V}}

For the second point, since

{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}_{\underline{V}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\underline{\mathcal{E}}_{\underline{V}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\underline{{\mathcal{D}}}_{\underline{V}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\underline{\presheaf}^{\mathcal{K}_{\underline{V}}}_{\mathcal{R}_{\underline{V}}}(\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}_{\underline{V}})}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces j}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces L_{\underline{V}}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces F}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces F^{\prime}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f^{\prime}}
\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f}

The transformation

. Then

\mathchoice{\mbox{\uline{\phantom{$\displaystyle\map$}}\hbox to0.0pt{\hss\color[rgb]{1,1,1}\hbox to0.0pt{\hskip 0.0pt\raisebox{0.5pt}[0.0pt]{$\displaystyle\map$}\hss}\hbox to0.0pt{\hskip and so taking the section over

6.5
The presentables–idempotents equivalence

We want to formulate the equivalence between presentables and idempotent-completes in the parametrised world, and so we need to introduce some definitions. To avoid potential confusion, we will for example use the terminology
parametrised
-accessibles instead of
{\mathcal{T}}
–accessibles to indicate that we take
{\mathcal{T}}_{/V}
–accessibles in the fibre over
V
.

Definition 6.5.1
.

Let
\kappa
be a regular cardinal.

•

Let
\underline{{\mathrm{Acc}}}_{{\mathcal{T}},\kappa}\subset\underline{\widehat{\mathrm{Cat}}}_{{\mathcal{T}}}
be the non-full
{\mathcal{T}}
–subcategory of
\kappa
-parametrised-accessible categories and
\kappa
-parametrised-accessible functors preserving
\kappa
-parametrised-compacts.

•

Let
\underline{\mathrm{Cat}}_{{\mathcal{T}}}^{\underline{\mathrm{Idem}}}\subseteq\underline{\widehat{\mathrm{Cat}}}_{{\mathcal{T}}}
be the full
{\mathcal{T}}
–subcategory on the small parametrised-idempotent-complete categories.

•

Let
\underline{{\mathrm{Cat}}}_{{\mathcal{T}}}^{\underline{\mathrm{rex}}(\kappa)}\subset\underline{\widehat{\mathrm{Cat}}}_{{\mathcal{T}}}
be the non-full subcategory whose objects are
\kappa
-parametrised–cocomplete small categories and morphisms those parametrised–functors that strongly preserve
\kappa
-small parametrised–colimits.

•

Let
\underline{\mathrm{Cat}}_{{\mathcal{T}}}^{\underline{\mathrm{Idem}}(\kappa)}\subseteq\underline{{\mathrm{Cat}}}_{{\mathcal{T}}}^{\underline{\mathrm{rex}}(\kappa)}
be the full subcategory whose objects are
\kappa
-parametrised–cocomplete small parametrised-idempotent-complete categories.

•

Let
\underline{\mathrm{Pr}}_{{\mathcal{T}},L,\kappa}\subset\underline{{\mathrm{Acc}}}_{{\mathcal{T}},\kappa}
be the non-full
{\mathcal{T}}
–subcategory whose objects are parametrised-presentables and whose morphisms are parametrised-left adjoints that preserve
\kappa
-parametrised-compacts.

•

Let
\underline{\mathrm{Pr}}_{{\mathcal{T}},R,\kappa\operatorname{-filt}}\subset\underline{\widehat{\mathrm{Cat}}}_{{\mathcal{T}}}
be the non-full
{\mathcal{T}}
–subcategory of parametrised presentable categories and morphisms the parametrised
\kappa
-accessible functors which strongly preserve parametrised limits.

Notation 6.5.2
.

Let
\underline{\func}_{{\mathcal{T}}}^{\underline{\kappa}}\subseteq\underline{\func}_{{\mathcal{T}}}
be the full subcategory of
\kappa
–
{\mathcal{T}}
–compact-preserving functors.

Lemma 6.5.3

(“
[
Lur09
, Prop. 5.4.2.17]
”)
.

Let
\kappa
be a regular cardinal. Then
(-)^{\underline{\kappa}}:\underline{{\mathrm{Acc}}}_{{\mathcal{T}},\kappa}\longrightarrow\underline{\widehat{\mathrm{Cat}}}_{{\mathcal{T}}}
induces an equivalence to
\underline{\mathrm{Cat}}_{{\mathcal{T}}}^{\underline{\mathrm{Idem}}}
, whose inverse
\underline{\mathrm{Cat}}_{{\mathcal{T}}}^{\underline{\mathrm{Idem}}}\rightarrow\underline{{\mathrm{Acc}}}_{{\mathcal{T}},\kappa}
is
\underline{\mathrm{Ind}}_{\kappa}
.

Proof.

To see
{\mathcal{T}}
–fully faithfulness,
3.5.4
gives

\begin{split}\underline{\func}_{{\mathcal{T}}}^{\kappa\operatorname{-filt},\underline{\kappa}}(\underline{\mathrm{Ind}}_{\kappa}\underline{{\mathcal{C}}},\underline{\mathrm{Ind}}_{\kappa}\underline{{\mathcal{D}}})&\xrightarrow{\simeq}\underline{\func}_{{\mathcal{T}}}^{\underline{\kappa}}(\underline{\mathrm{Ind}}_{\kappa}(\underline{{\mathcal{C}}})^{\underline{\kappa}},\underline{\mathrm{Ind}}_{\kappa}\underline{{\mathcal{D}}})\\
&\xrightarrow{\simeq}\underline{\func}_{{\mathcal{T}}}(\underline{\mathrm{Ind}}_{\kappa}(\underline{{\mathcal{C}}})^{\underline{\kappa}},\underline{\mathrm{Ind}}_{\kappa}(\underline{{\mathcal{D}}})^{\underline{\kappa}})\end{split}

where we have also used, by
5.3.2
(1), that
\underline{\mathrm{Ind}}_{\kappa}(\underline{\mathrm{Ind}}_{\kappa}(\underline{{\mathcal{C}}})^{\underline{\kappa}})\simeq\underline{\mathrm{Ind}}_{\kappa}\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}
. As for the essential image, let
\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}
be a small
{\mathcal{T}}
–idempotent-complete category. Then by
5.3.2
(2) we know that
\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}\simeq\underline{\mathrm{Ind}}_{\kappa}(\underline{{\mathcal{C}}})^{\underline{\kappa}}
, and so it is in the essential image as required. Finally to see the statement about the inverse, just note that we already have the functors and the appropriate natural transformations on compositions. Then using
5.3.2
again, we see that the transformations are pointwise equivalences, and so equivalences.
∎

Theorem 6.5.4

(
{\mathcal{T}}
–presentable-idempotent correspondence, “
[
Lur09
, Prop. 5.5.7.8 and Rmk. 5.5.7.9]
”)
.

Let
\kappa
be a regular cardinal. Then

(-)^{\underline{\kappa}}:\underline{\mathrm{Pr}}_{{\mathcal{T}},L,\kappa}\longrightarrow\underline{\widehat{\mathrm{Cat}}}_{{\mathcal{T}}}^{\underline{\mathrm{rex}}(\kappa)}
is
{\mathcal{T}}
–fully faithful with essential image
\underline{\mathrm{Cat}}_{{\mathcal{T}}}^{\underline{\mathrm{Idem}}(\kappa)}
, and inverse
\underline{\mathrm{Cat}}_{{\mathcal{T}}}^{\underline{\mathrm{Idem}}(\kappa)}\rightarrow\underline{\mathrm{Pr}}_{{\mathcal{T}},L,\kappa}
given by
\underline{\mathrm{Ind}}_{\kappa}
.

Proof.

That it is
{\mathcal{T}}
–fully faithful with the specified essential image is by
6.5.3
together with
5.1.6
and
6.2.2
. That the inverse from
6.5.3
via
\underline{\mathrm{Ind}}_{\kappa}
lands in
{\mathcal{T}}
–presentables is by
6.1.2
(4).
∎

6.6
Indexed products of presentables

The purpose of this subsection is to show that the (non-full) inclusions
\underline{\mathrm{Pr}}_{{\mathcal{T}},L,\kappa},\underline{\mathrm{Pr}}_{{\mathcal{T}},R,\kappa\operatorname{-filt}}\subset\underline{\widehat{\mathrm{Cat}}}_{{\mathcal{T}}}
create indexed products.

Lemma 6.6.1

(Indexed products of
{\mathcal{T}}
–presentables)
.

Let
f:W\rightarrow V
be in
{\mathcal{T}}
and
\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}
be a
{\mathcal{T}}_{/W}
–presentable category. Then
f_{*}\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}
is a
{\mathcal{T}}_{/V}
–presentable category.

Proof.

We first note that if
\underline{{\mathcal{D}}}
is a
{\mathcal{T}}_{/W}
–category, then
f_{*}\underline{\func}_{\underline{W}}(\underline{{\mathcal{D}}},\underline{\mathcal{S}}_{\underline{W}})\simeq\underline{\func}_{\underline{V}}(f_{!}\underline{{\mathcal{D}}},\underline{\mathcal{S}}_{\underline{V}}).
To see this, let
\underline{\mathcal{E}}
be a
{\mathcal{T}}_{/V}
–category. Then

\begin{split}\map_{\mathrm{Cat}_{{\mathcal{T}}_{/V}}}(\underline{\mathcal{E}},f_{*}\underline{\func}_{\underline{W}}(\underline{{\mathcal{D}}},\underline{\mathcal{S}}_{\underline{W}}))&\simeq\map_{\mathrm{Cat}_{{\mathcal{T}}_{/W}}}(f^{*}\underline{\mathcal{E}},\underline{\func}_{\underline{W}}(\underline{{\mathcal{D}}},\underline{\mathcal{S}}_{\underline{W}}))\\
&\simeq\map_{\mathrm{Cat}_{{\mathcal{T}}_{/W}}}(\underline{{\mathcal{D}}},\underline{\func}_{\underline{W}}(f^{*}\underline{\mathcal{E}},\underline{\mathcal{S}}_{\underline{W}}))\\
&\simeq\map_{\mathrm{Cat}_{{\mathcal{T}}_{/W}}}(\underline{{\mathcal{D}}},f^{*}\underline{\func}_{\underline{V}}(\underline{\mathcal{E}},\underline{\mathcal{S}}_{\underline{V}}))\\
&\simeq\map_{\mathrm{Cat}_{{\mathcal{T}}_{/V}}}(f_{!}\underline{{\mathcal{D}}},\underline{\func}_{\underline{V}}(\underline{\mathcal{E}},\underline{\mathcal{S}}_{\underline{V}}))\\
&\simeq\map_{\mathrm{Cat}_{{\mathcal{T}}_{/V}}}(\underline{\mathcal{E}},\underline{\func}_{\underline{V}}(f_{!}\underline{{\mathcal{D}}},\underline{\mathcal{S}}_{\underline{V}}))\end{split}

By
6.1.2
we have a accessible
{\mathcal{T}}_{/W}
–Bousfield localisation
\underline{\func}_{\underline{W}}(\underline{{\mathcal{D}}},\underline{\mathcal{S}}_{\underline{W}})\rightleftarrows\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}
for some small
{\mathcal{T}}_{/W}
–category
\underline{{\mathcal{D}}}
. Hence by
4.3.2
, we obtain the accessible adjunction
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\underline{\func}_{\underline{V}}(f_{!}\underline{{\mathcal{D}}},\underline{\mathcal{S}}_{\underline{V}})\simeq f_{*}\underline{\func}_{\underline{W}}(\underline{{\mathcal{D}}},\underline{\mathcal{S}}_{\underline{W}})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces f_{*}\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}}

Therefore,
f_{*}\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}
must be
{\mathcal{T}}_{/V}
–presentable, again by
6.1.2
.
∎

Proposition 6.6.2

(Creation of indexed products for presentables)
.

The (non-full) inclusions
\underline{\mathrm{Pr}}_{{\mathcal{T}},L,\kappa},\underline{\mathrm{Pr}}_{{\mathcal{T}},R,\kappa\operatorname{-filt}}\subset\underline{\widehat{\mathrm{Cat}}}_{{\mathcal{T}}}

6.7
Functor categories and tensors of presentables

In this final subsection, we record several basic results about the interaction between parametrised-presentability and functor categories, totally analogous to the unparametrised setting.

Lemma 6.7.1

(Small cotensors preserve
{\mathcal{T}}
–presentability)
.

Let
\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}
be a small
\>{{\mathcal{T}}}
-category and
\underline{{\mathcal{D}}}
be
{\mathcal{T}}
–presentable. Then
\underline{\func}_{{\mathcal{T}}}(\underline{{\mathcal{C}}},\underline{{\mathcal{D}}})
is also
{\mathcal{T}}
–presentable.

Proof.

As a special case, suppose first that
\underline{{\mathcal{D}}}\simeq\underline{\presheaf}_{{\mathcal{T}}}(\underline{{\mathcal{D}}}^{\prime})
for a small
{\mathcal{T}}
–category
\underline{{\mathcal{D}}}^{\prime}

Lemma 6.7.2

(“
[
Lur09
, Lem. 5.5.4.17]
”)
.

Let
F:\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}\rightleftarrows\underline{{\mathcal{D}}}:G
be a
{\mathcal{T}}
–adjunction between
{\mathcal{T}}
–presentables. Suppose we have a
{\mathcal{T}}
–accessible Bousfield localisation
L:\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}\rightleftarrows\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}^{0}:i
. Let
\underline{{\mathcal{D}}}^{0}\coloneqq G^{-1}(\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}^{0})\subseteq\underline{{\mathcal{D}}}
. Then we have a
{\mathcal{T}}
–accessible Bousfield localisation
L^{\prime}:\underline{{\mathcal{D}}}\rightleftarrows\underline{{\mathcal{D}}}^{0}:i^{\prime}
.

Proof.

The
{\mathcal{T}}
–accessibility of the Bousfield localisation
L:\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}\rightleftarrows\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}^{0}:i
ensures that there is a small set of morphisms of
\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}
such that
\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}^{0}
are precisely the
S
-local objects. Then it is easy to see that
\underline{{\mathcal{D}}}^{0}\subseteq\underline{{\mathcal{D}}}
is precisely the
F(S)
-local
{\mathcal{T}}
–subcategory by using the adjunction.
∎

Lemma 6.7.3

(“
[
Lur09
, Lem. 5.5.4.18]
”)
.

Let
\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}
be a
{\mathcal{T}}
–presentable category and
\{\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}_{a}\}_{a\in A}
be a family of
{\mathcal{T}}
–accessible Bousfield local subcategories indexed by a small set
A
. Then
\bigcap_{a\in A}\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}_{a}
is also a
{\mathcal{T}}
–accessible Bousfield local subcategory.

Proof.

This is because, if we write
S(a)
for the morphisms of
\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}
such that
\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}_{a}
is the
S(a)
-local objects, then
\bigcap_{a\in A}\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}_{a}
are the
\bigcup_{a\in A}S(a)
-local objects.
∎

For the remaining results, recall from
3.3.10
that
\underline{\func}_{{\mathcal{T}}}^{R}
and
\underline{\func}_{{\mathcal{T}}}^{L}
denote strongly
{\mathcal{T}}
–limit- and
{\mathcal{T}}
–colimit-preserving functors, respectively, and
\underline{\rfunc}_{{\mathcal{T}}}
and
\underline{\lfunc}_{{\mathcal{T}}}
denote
{\mathcal{T}}
–right and
{\mathcal{T}}
–left adjoint functors, respectively.

to0.0pt{\hskip-0.46193pt\raisebox{0.19133pt}[0.0pt]{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{op}$}\hss}\hbox to0.0pt{\hskip-0.35355pt\raisebox{0.35355pt}[0.0pt]{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{op}$}\hss}\hbox to0.0pt{\hskip-0.19133pt\raisebox{0.46193pt}[0.0pt]{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{op}$}\hss}\mbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathrm{op}$}}}}}},\underline{{\mathcal{D}}})}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\underline{\mathcal{E}}}
{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\underline{\func}_{{\mathcal{T}}}(\tconstant_{\mathcal{T}}(\Delta^{1}),\underline{{\mathcal{D}}})}

\lrcorner

\scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\mathrm{ev}_{\alpha}}

where
\underline{\mathcal{E}}
is the full subcategory spanned by the equivalences. Hence by
6.7.2
it will suffice to show that
\underline{\mathcal{E}}\subseteq\underline{\func}_{{\mathcal{T}}}(\tconstant_{\mathcal{T}}(\Delta^{1}),\underline{{\mathcal{D}}})
is a
{\mathcal{T}}
–accessible Bousfield localisation. But this is clear since it is just given by the
{\mathcal{T}}
–left Kan extension along
\ast\rightarrow\Delta^{1}
.

The statement for
\underline{\func}_{{\mathcal{T}}}^{L}(\underline{{\mathcal{C}}},\underline{{\mathcal{D}}})
is proved analogously, but without having to take opposites in showing that
L^{*}:\underline{\func}^{L}_{{\mathcal{T}}}(S^{-1}\underline{\presheaf}_{{\mathcal{T}}}(\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}^{\prime}),\underline{{\mathcal{D}}})\rightarrow\underline{\func}_{{\mathcal{T}}}^{L,S^{-1}}(\underline{\presheaf}_{{\mathcal{T}}}(\underline{{\mathcal{C}}}^{\prime}),{\mathcal{D}})
is an equivalence.
∎

The following result was stated as Example 3.26 in
[
Nar17
]
without proof, and so we prove it here. Here the tensor product is the one constructed in
[
Nar17
,
\lx@sectionsign 3.4
]
.
